question.text: Given an A.P. and a G.P. with positive terms, with the first and second terms of the progressions being equal. If $a_n$ and $b_n$ be the $n^{\text {th }}$ term of A.P. and G.P. respectively then

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Hint: } a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots \ldots, a_n \rightarrow \text { AP } \\ & a_1, a_2, b_3, \ldots \ldots, b_n \rightarrow G P \\ & a_n=a_1+(n-1)\left(a_2-a_1\right) \\ & b_n=a_1\left(\frac{a_2}{a_1}\right)^{n-1}=a_2^{n-1} \cdot a_1^{1-n+1}=a_2^{n-1} \cdot a_1^{2-n} \\ & \text { for } n=3, a_3=a_1+2\left(a_2-a_1\right) \Rightarrow a_3=2 a_2-a_1 \\ & b_3=a_2^2 \cdot a_1^{-1}=\frac{a_2^2}{a_1} \\ & a_3-b_3=2 a_2-a_1-\frac{a_2^2}{a_1}=\frac{2 a_2 a_1-a_1^2-a_2^2}{a_1}=\frac{2 a_1 a_2-\left(a_1^2+a_2^2\right)}{a_1} \lt 0 \quad\left[\because a_1^2+a_2^2 \gt 2 a_1 a_2\right] \\ & \therefore a_3 \lt b_3 \therefore a_n \lt b_n \text { for all } n \gt 2\end{aligned}$
